multipleChoice.question: Where are James and Salome when they have their conversation in Part A?
options: In the house in the shade
Beside the well in the shade
In the field under a tree
On the road near the village
multipleChoice.explanation: The story says they are speaking beside the well in the shade while the sun scorches the earth.

multipleChoice.question: According to James, how does the relationship between us and Jesus compare to branches and a vine?
options: As servants remain in a house
As branches remain in a vine, so we remain in Jesus Christ
As farmers remain in a field
As sheep remain with the hired hand
multipleChoice.explanation: James says that if we remain in Jesus Christ and he in us, just as branches remain in the vine, Jesus says we are his friends.

multipleChoice.question: How does Jesus regard us, according to James?
options: As slaves who do not know his will
As servants who must earn his favor
As friends, not slaves
As strangers who must be taught
multipleChoice.explanation: Jesus does not consider us slaves but friends. A slave does not know what his master does, but a friend knows.

multipleChoice.question: What is God described as in Part A?
options: The shepherd
The farmer
Love
The light
multipleChoice.explanation: The story states clearly: God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God.

multipleChoice.question: What is Jesus's commandment according to this chapter?
options: That we remain in the field
That we love one another as friends love one another
That we guard the sheep
That we know the shepherd's voice
multipleChoice.explanation: The commandment of Jesus is that we love one another just as friends love one another.

multipleChoice.question: According to James, what happens when we remain in Jesus's love?
options: We receive great wealth
We become shepherds
His joy is in us
The sun no longer scorches us
multipleChoice.explanation: Whenever we remain in his love, his joy is in us.

multipleChoice.question: What does James say about someone who claims to love God but hates his brother?
options: He is a faithful servant
He is a liar
He is a hired hand
He is a stranger
multipleChoice.explanation: If someone says 'I love God' and hates his brother, he is a liar. The one who does not love his brother whom he sees cannot love God whom he does not see.

multipleChoice.question: What does Jesus place in our hearts, according to James?
options: Fear
His commandments
His love
The knowledge of the shepherd
multipleChoice.explanation: Jesus places his love in our hearts.

multipleChoice.question: What does Jesus declare about himself that James quotes in Part B?
options: I am the hired hand
I am the good shepherd
I am the farmer
I am the wolf
multipleChoice.explanation: James quotes Jesus saying: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

multipleChoice.question: What does the hired hand do when he sees the wolf coming?
options: He guards the sheep bravely
He calls out to the shepherd
He abandons the sheep and flees
He takes the sheep to safety
multipleChoice.explanation: The hired hand sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep, and flees, because the sheep are not his own.

multipleChoice.question: According to James, why does the hired hand not care about the sheep?
options: Because he fears the shepherd
Because the sheep do not belong to him
Because he loves only the wolf
Because the shepherd told him not to care
multipleChoice.explanation: The hired hand does not care about the sheep because he only loves money; the sheep are not his own.

multipleChoice.question: How does the good shepherd know his own sheep, according to James?
options: Just as the Father knows Jesus and Jesus knows the Father
Just as a farmer knows his field
Just as a stranger knows the road
Just as the sun knows the earth
multipleChoice.explanation: The good shepherd knows his own and his own know him, just as the Father knows Jesus and he knows the Father.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Salome marvel in Part B?
options: Because the shepherd guards so many sheep
Because the hired hand fled from the wolf
Because Jesus lays down his life for people
Because the sun is so hot
multipleChoice.explanation: Salome marvels and asks: 'Jesus lays down his life for people? Why does he do this?' She is amazed by this act of love.

multipleChoice.question: According to James, why does the Father love Jesus?
options: Because Jesus guards the sheepfold
Because Jesus lays down his life so he can take it again
Because Jesus feeds the sheep
Because Jesus knows the hired hands
multipleChoice.explanation: The Father loves Jesus because he lays down his life in order to take it again.

multipleChoice.question: What is said about Jesus's authority over his own life?
options: Someone else takes his life from him
The Father forces him to give it
He has authority to lay it down and to take it again
Only the hired hand can take it
multipleChoice.explanation: No one takes his life from him; rather, he lays it down of himself. He has authority to lay it down and authority to take it again.

multipleChoice.question: What does James say is the reason we are able to love one another?
options: Because the shepherd commands it
Because we are strong enough
Because Jesus himself loves us
Because love is easy
multipleChoice.explanation: We are able to love one another and Jesus because he himself loves us, and he shows us how to love one another.

multipleChoice.question: According to James, what does perfect love cast out?
options: The hired hand
Fear
The wolf
Darkness
multipleChoice.explanation: Perfect love casts out fear, for there is no fear in love.

trueFalse.statement: James and Salome are speaking beside the well in the shade.
trueFalse.explanation: The story places them beside the well in the shade while the sun shines brightly in the sky.

trueFalse.statement: Jesus considers us slaves rather than friends.
trueFalse.explanation: Jesus does not consider us slaves but friends. A slave does not know what his master does, but a friend knows.

trueFalse.statement: God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God.
trueFalse.explanation: The story states: God is love, and the person who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.

trueFalse.statement: The commandment of Jesus is that we love one another.
trueFalse.explanation: This is the commandment of Jesus: that we love one another just as friends love one another.

trueFalse.statement: The sun is resting and the weather is cool when James and Salome speak.
trueFalse.explanation: The sun shines very brightly in the sky and scorches the earth and the farmers in the fields.

trueFalse.statement: The sheep in the field eat the grass while the shepherd watches over them.
trueFalse.explanation: The sheep eat the grass, and the shepherd watches over them; the shepherd guards the sheep.

trueFalse.statement: A person who hates his brother can still truly love God.
trueFalse.explanation: Anyone who says 'I love God' and hates his brother is a liar. One cannot love God whom he does not see while failing to love his brother whom he does see.

trueFalse.statement: Jesus places his love in our hearts.
trueFalse.explanation: Jesus places his love in our hearts.

trueFalse.statement: The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
trueFalse.explanation: Jesus himself says: I am the good shepherd, and the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

trueFalse.statement: The hired hand guards the sheep bravely when the wolf comes.
trueFalse.explanation: The hired hand sees the wolf coming and abandons the sheep and flees, because the sheep are not his own and he does not care about them.

trueFalse.statement: The hired hand works for money rather than out of love for the sheep.
trueFalse.explanation: The hired hand is a person who works in order to receive money; the sheep are not his own, so he does not truly care for them.

trueFalse.statement: The wolf seizes and scatters the sheep when the hired hand flees.
trueFalse.explanation: The wolf seizes and scatters the sheep, because the hired hand flees and does not protect them.

trueFalse.statement: No one is able to take Jesus's life from him against his will.
trueFalse.explanation: No one takes his life from him; rather, he himself lays it down of his own will. He has authority to lay it down and to take it again.

trueFalse.statement: James says we are the sheep of Jesus and he is our shepherd.
trueFalse.explanation: James says: we are his sheep and he is our shepherd. We are known by him and he is known by us.

trueFalse.statement: There is great fear inside perfect love.
trueFalse.explanation: Perfect love casts out fear. There is no fear in love.

trueFalse.statement: The Father loves Jesus because Jesus lays down his life for the sheep.
trueFalse.explanation: The Father loves Jesus because he lays down his life in order to take it again.

trueFalse.statement: James answers Salome's wonder about the cross by saying Jesus does it because of fear.
trueFalse.explanation: James says Jesus lays down his life because of love. Jesus loves us, and greater love than this no one has.

yesNo.question: Does James say that we are friends of Jesus?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. Jesus says we are his friends, not slaves. A friend knows what the master does; a slave does not.

yesNo.question: Can a person truly love God while hating his brother?
yesNo.explanation: No. Anyone who says he loves God but hates his brother is a liar. One who does not love the brother he sees cannot love God whom he does not see.

yesNo.question: Does the sun scorch the earth and the farmers in the fields?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The sun shines very brightly in the sky and scorches the earth and the farmers in the fields.

yesNo.question: Are we able to love one another because Jesus loves us?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. We are able to love one another and Jesus because he himself loves us first and shows us how.

yesNo.question: Does James say that God is love?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The story says directly: God is love. The one who remains in love remains in God.

yesNo.question: Does the hired hand lay down his life for the sheep?
yesNo.explanation: No. The hired hand abandons the sheep and flees when the wolf comes. Only the good shepherd lays down his life.

yesNo.question: Does Jesus know his own sheep?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The good shepherd knows his own and his own know him, just as the Father knows Jesus and Jesus knows the Father.

yesNo.question: Does Salome marvel at the teaching that Jesus lays down his life?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. Salome marvels and asks why Jesus would lay down his life for people.

yesNo.question: Does perfect love cast out fear?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. Perfect love casts out fear, for there is no fear in love.

yesNo.question: Does the hired hand care about the sheep as much as the shepherd does?
yesNo.explanation: No. The hired hand cares only about money. He does not care about the sheep because they are not his own.

yesNo.question: Does James say that no one has greater love than to lay down his life for his friends?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. Greater love than this no one has: whoever lays down his life for his friends has great love.
